caption:
Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia's president and CEO and left the board, effective immediately.
CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while the board looks for a permanent one. Nvidia gave no reason.
The stock fell more than 11% before the market opened.

paragraphs.text: Jensen Huang has resigned as president and chief executive of Nvidia, the company confirmed on Thursday, November 12, 2026, according to TechCrunch. Cointelegraph reported that he also gave up his seat on the board and that the resignation took effect immediately. Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and had led it ever since, a run of 33 years.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO until a permanent successor is named, and she keeps her role as CFO, both outlets reported. According to Cointelegraph, the board is considering internal and external candidates for the permanent job.

A regulatory filing cited by TechCrunch says the board accepted Huang's resignation on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, one day before the public announcement. In its statement the company thanked Huang for his contributions to Nvidia and to the industry, TechCrunch reported.

The board also named Harvey Jones as its chair. He is the managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and a former chief executive of Synopsys, and he has been an Nvidia director since 1993, according to TechCrunch. He is the first chair the board has had. Fortune reported a day earlier that the board had no chair and that the company had no clear succession plan.
No reason given, after a week of scandal

Neither report gives a reason for the resignation, and neither quotes Huang. The departure follows several days of damaging headlines. TechCrunch wrote that Huang had admitted to a romantic affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. Reuters, citing The Wall Street Journal, reported on November 11 that the board was preparing to remove him, and noted a New York Times report that Huang had also had a relationship with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. Reuters said at the time that it could not immediately verify those reports.

Investors reacted before the market opened. Nvidia shares fell more than 11 percent in premarket trading on Thursday, according to TechCrunch. Since the scandal broke, the company has lost more than $300 billion in market value, TechCrunch and Reuters reported.

Huang was unusually central to how Nvidia runs. Fortune reported that he had about 60 direct reports and sat at the middle of most decisions. That structure now passes, at least for a while, to a finance chief who is doing two jobs at once.

NeuraFeed's reading: this is one of the biggest leadership changes the AI industry has faced. Nvidia's chips sit under nearly every major AI model, and for three decades the company's strategy and its public voice were the same person. An interim CEO who is also the CFO signals that the board moved quickly and without a successor ready. The appointment of a first chair suggests directors want more distance between the board and whoever runs the company next. Customers and rivals will read the choice of a permanent CEO as a statement about whether Nvidia keeps its current course.
Watch for the board's choice of a permanent CEO and whether it comes from inside Nvidia, and for Huang's own first public statement, which neither report includes.
